target_customer: Consumers and groups booking cooking, baking and tasting classes; restaurants and hotels supply venues and chefs
problem: Traditional cooking classes are expensive and intensive, and restaurants have idle space and chef time that could be monetized.
business_model: Marketplace: per-class ticket fee (about $55 at launch), with fixed chef fees and venue minimums

founders.name: Billy Guan
founders.background_notes: A Columbia directory snippet in search results calls him a Columbia alumnus; the page was not opened, so education is not recorded.

founders.name: Helen Sun
founders.background_notes: Named as cofounder in the TechCrunch July 2017 article and on the YC page. Background not found.

competitors.name: Cookly
competitors.what: Online marketplace pitched as the Airbnb of cooking classes, listing cooking schools abroad
competitors.traction_then: 17 cooking schools in Indonesia in 2016, with plans for more countries

competitors.name: VizEat
competitors.what: Peer-to-peer marketplace for home-cooked meals and cooking classes with amateur chefs
competitors.funding_then: EUR 3.8M raised the previous September (2016) per a May 2017 article

competitors.name: Sur la Table
competitors.what: Retailer running in-store cooking classes, used by TechCrunch as the price benchmark (close to $100 per person)

technical_complexity.rationale: A booking marketplace with reviews. Standard web engineering; the difficulty was operational supply and demand.

defensibility.rationale: Venue and chef relationships help, but classes are easy to replicate and customers can book elsewhere.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Airbnb launched Experiences around 2016 to 2017 and a dedicated cooking category in November 2019. CocuSocial is still listed Active; no acquisition found.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in July 2017 reported about 35 classes a month a year after launch, priced at $55 versus close to $100 at Sur la Table. No spend data beyond that.

branding.domain_note: Uses cocusocial.com, an exact-match domain for the name.

identity.voice_and_tone: Social and casual, aimed at couples and group events per the site title

brand_strength.rationale: No brand-focused press found; the name is a coined blend of social and a Spanish-sounding prefix with unknown origin.

outcome_analysis: CocuSocial launched a New York class marketplace around 2016 and joined YC in Summer 2017 with about 35 classes a month. The directory still lists it as active, with a small team. No institutional funding round was found, so it appears to have stayed small and capital light, but its trajectory after 2017 is not documented in sources found.
notes: Company website fetch returned only a page title, so the site content was not verified. Aggregators report seed of about $120K to $240K (CB Insights, Simplify, Caplight) at differing totals; unverified and not recorded as a round. The YC page lists Vancouver while other sources say New York; the TechCrunch piece says live in New York. Outcome and shutdown search returned nothing relevant. The 120K USD Aug 2017 round (Y Combinator, listed by CB Insights as a seed dated 2017-08-23) rests on a single database, CB Insights; Seedtable shows the same 120K in Aug 2017 but its investor split is modeled, so it is not independent. Recorded as other because it is the YC standard investment. Other aggregator totals up to 240K remain unverified.
